newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NTT says to go international in July/August.
newsitem.headline: NTT says to go international in July/August.

text.p: Japanese telecommunications giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said on Monday it would form a unit, possibly as soon as July, to start international services.
"We plan to start international services in the autumn," said executive manager Masanobu Suzuki of NTT, which is now restricted by law to domestic services.
"We need to form a new unit in July, or early August at latest," he told a news conference
Japan's parliament is expected to approve a change in the law to allow NTT's entry into the international market by the middle of next week.
NTT has said that it would focus on three areas in its international strategy.
It plans to provide Japanese multinationals abroad with information and systems integration services.
It will also seek telecommunications licenses in Europe, the United States and Asia to provide the companies with seamless voice and date service.
NTT will also invest in local networks.
NTT has earmarked a budget of 100 billion yen for overseas projects in the 1997/98 business year.
